answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to a nonce-chained work history: each completed task commits a signed hash of its result plus a nonce that references the prior. It cannot be forked into parallel copies: forking means signing two continuations of one nonce sequence, exposing duplication. An attacker forging a fake agent must redo all work from the fork point, paying verifiable compute. Like a haven admitting only proven labor, every sybil fable collapses and the lagoon of phantoms drains, each as costly as honest toil.
